Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear questions, and great context on session characteristics — that helps a lot. I've attached our Q4 rate card and a short CSV with a worked example based on the numbers you provided. High level summary below, then the example numbers.

Quick primer (short):
- Chat Completions (chat-completions endpoint): billed per token (input + output). Tokenization is standard; example: ~4 chars/token for English. Both prompt context (conversation history) and generated tokens count toward the billed tokens.
- Responses (responses endpoint): billed per response unit. We designed Responses to simplify some common app patterns: a single API call can produce structured outputs, tool calls, and content. Billing is expressed as a combination of request tokens + generated tokens but presented in the rate card as "response units" to simplify quoting — each model maps to a token-equivalent multiplier. Practically, you can treat 1 response unit ~= X tokens for cost estimation (we include that mapping in the attached CSV).
- Legacy completions / embeddings endpoints: remain token-based; embeddings are billed per vector unit (per 1,024 tokens equivalent) on the rate card.

Worked example (from the CSV attached):
- Input: 350 chars ~ ~88 tokens (assuming ~4 chars/token)
- Output (assistant reply): average 420 chars ~ ~105 tokens
- Conversation history: if you include last 3 turns on average, add ~300 tokens of context per call
- Chat Completions cost (per interaction): price_per_token * (input + context + output) => price_per_token * ~493 tokens
- Responses cost (per interaction): price_per_response_unit * 1.0 where 1 response unit maps to ~480 tokens for the selected model; so costs are similar but Responses simplifies line items and supports structured outputs with fewer round trips.

Key practical notes:
- If you send the full conversation each time, token counts drive cost. Using prefix caching or sending deltas reduces chat-completions billable tokens. Redwood's runtime supports KV caching and partial context to reduce repeated context cost — we can show estimated savings in a follow-up run.
- For pricing, we quote both token and response-unit rates in the rate card; when we do a committed-usage deal, we lock in the mapping and provide per-unit discounts so your invoice is predictable.

2) I can propose two committed tiers (12 mo): 10% off at $30k/mo commit, 18% off at $75k/mo commit. Marissa (cc) will own the formal pricing proposal.
3) Quick 30‑minute call to walk procurement through the rate card and the mapping table — are you available Thurs 12/3 11:00–11:30 PT?
